comments.author: @andrejslubkans7506
comments.text: Thank you very much for creating this beautiful informative video of my ancestral country.  I would like to point out two pronunciation rules of Latvian:  1) The letter "j" is pronounced like the "y" in the English word "yes".  In this respect the Latvian "j" is like the "j" in German, the Scandinavian languages, Polish, Lithuanian, Estonian, Finnish, Czech, Slovak et al.  2) Latvian is a first-syllable stress language with very few exceptions.  Thus the proper names in this video such as Liepaja and Kuldiga are stressed on the beginning syllable.   Another comment:  The video is a very poetic, serene and idyllic presentation of Latvian towns and country scenes.  I noticed some mention of German crusaders and merchants, but the country's history is sanitized.  In reality, the regions that comprise modern Latvia were brutally conquered by German crusaders and mostly oppressed by the Baltic German landowning class into the 20th century.  Poland-Lithuania, Sweden, Czarist Russia and the USSR fought devastating wars over this land, so that I am amazed that the people and the culture have succeeded in physically surviving the horrors of centuries of foreign conquest and oppression.  Again, thank you for your efforts to better acquaint the outside world with Latvia and its people.
